slides.subtitle: 10 minutes a week. Prompts included.
slides.highlight: Bad review? Step 4 has the prompt

slides.label: Why bother
slides.detail: 85% of UK shoppers check at least one review site before they buy (Feefo and Censuswide, 3,000 UK consumers). People read the stars, then they read how you replied.
slides.start: Google tells the reviewer when you reply, so the thank-you lands.

slides.label: Step 1: Write your house style
slides.detail: Paste: You write Google review replies for [business], a [what you do] in [town]. Tone: [friendly and plain]. Under 60 words. Thank them by first name, mention one thing they said, sign off as [name].
slides.start: Add: never say "we value your feedback". Save it in a note.

slides.label: Step 2: Gather the week's reviews
slides.detail: Pick one slot a week. Open your Business Profile, select Read reviews, and copy the new ones with each reviewer's first name and stars.
slides.start: Five reviews take about two minutes to gather.

slides.label: Step 3: Paste the batch prompt
slides.detail: Paste your house style, then: Here are this week's reviews. Write one reply for each, numbered to match. Short and warm for 4 and 5 stars. If anything is unclear, ask me first.
slides.start: You get every draft in seconds. Edit, do not rewrite.

slides.label: Step 4: The bad review
slides.detail: Paste this when a review stings:
slides.start: Wait ten minutes before you post it.
slides.quote: Thank them, own what we got wrong without arguing, no private details, invite them to call [number]. No excuses. Under 70 words.

slides.label: Step 5: Post the replies
slides.detail: In Business Profile, select Reply next to each review, paste the edited draft, select Reply. Your profile must be verified, and Google checks replies before they show.
slides.start: You can edit or delete a reply later.

slides.label: What it could give back
slides.detail: Five reviews a week at four minutes each by hand is 20 minutes. With the house style and one batch prompt, about 10. That is roughly 8 hours a year, and every review answered. Illustrative, so time your own.
slides.start: The bigger win: the next customer sees you answer.

slides.label: One thing to watch
slides.detail: Read every reply before it goes out. ChatGPT can miss sarcasm or promise something you would not. Works on the free plan, because you only paste text.
